title: Console feature rebaseline: cut nonessential dashboard/tracing/cost surfaces
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD rebaseline and acceptance criteria for a reduced-scope Console surface that delivers immediate value while deferring higher-effort visuals and deep trace analysis. Goal: ship a coherent first pass of dashboards, light tracing links, and per-route cost breakdowns within the Q1 shipment window with a clear path for follow-on enhancements.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: surface a single configurable dashboard per org with 3 baseline cards (request throughput, error rate, and 7-day cost by route). Each card must have tooltip text and link to the route-level inspector.
Tracing: implement a lightweight 'jump to trace' link from an error-level card that opens an external or internal trace view; do NOT implement full inline trace timeline or span waterfall in MVP.
Cost breakdown: provide per-route 7-day and 30-day aggregated token and dollar spend with simple top-10 table; exclude category-level attribution and multi-dimensional filters for MVP.
Rollout: feature gated behind console-beta feature flag with a 10% internal canary rollout and telemetry capturing usage of each card and trace-link clicks.
Performance: dashboard queries must render within 1.5s p50 for orgs with <100k requests/day; fallback UX for timeouts (explain what to retry) must be present.
Observability: emit event types for card loads, card errors, trace-link clicks, and cost-card exports to allow post-launch tuning.
UX: Figma designs approved by Design (see links) and annotated acceptance states for empty and error cases.
Docs: Console docs page and quickstart updated before rollout, including brief description of limitations and roadmap for follow-ons.
QA: end-to-end tests covering dashboard load, card interactions, trace-link opens, and basic cost aggregation correctness (sampled test org).
decisions: Cut inline trace timeline: will ship a link to the existing tracing system instead of building a new embedded timeline for MVP.
Limit dashboard to one configurable page: reduces backend query surface and avoids layout complexity for first launch.
Defer advanced cost attribution and filters: prioritized core per-route spend so we can validate value before investing in multi-dimensional cost models.
Use existing metrics pipeline (no new telemetry schema) for initial rollout; add metric schema changes in follow-on sprint if needed.
Require a feature flaged canary sequence with internal sign-off before enabling for customers.
notes: Trade-offs: This cut reduces immediate developer UX by not surfacing deep trace timelines and advanced filter combos, but materially reduces implementation risk and time to first product delivery.
If we see >20% trace-link click-through from canary telemetry, schedule follow-up sprint to prototype embedded trace timeline (ENG spike request).
Design flagged two low-effort polish items (hover previews on cost rows, condensed mobile card) that can be included if schedule allows; prioritize mobile condensing only for accessibility reasons.
Backend changes required: a new aggregated per-route cost table (daily granularity) and a lightweight dashboard query endpoint with request timeouts and caching. Work owned by ENG-8921.
Known risk: orgs with >1M requests/day may exceed the 1.5s target; plan to mitigate via cache TTL tuning and optional precomputed rollups in a follow-on release.
